checks.name: Source explicitly identifies this as a new restoration; it does not reuse the lost implementation hash or old test credit.
Only the fixed public repository and exact evidence ref, commit, tree and parent are allowed by production constants.
The working bare repository must be a new canonical path; existing archives are never overwritten and exact existing outputs are reverified against actual Git bytes.
Every Git command retains complete stdout/stderr files, stdin, arguments, return code and byte/SHA descriptors; binary stdout is streamed to avoid decoding corruption.
All local Git reads disable replacement objects and implicit promisor lazy fetch; production network actions are explicit fetch or ls-remote only.
Normal authentication and global/system Git configuration remain available; only declared performance and routing controls are changed in the newly created local bare repository.
The four metadata files are pinned by exact lengths, SHA256 and commit-tree object IDs.
The actual published base archive-parts directory contains exactly the 29 expected part files, with no README or other entry; the published base evidence directory has no original-assets directory.
The production tree scope must contain exactly 409 archive paths, four metadata paths and seven auxiliary paths; no loose path acceptance is used.
Every archive descriptor must equal the original frozen PLAN index/offset/bytes/SHA256/Git blob SHA; concatenated size is fixed.
cat-file batch headers, exact payload bytes, separators and end-of-stream are checked; each part receives independent SHA256 and Git blob SHA verification.
The assembled 490564596-byte archive must match whole SHA256 066a46e41e34578a2adbf2a1120e8aba0470dfde44d6052bc8576d8fcb9aa212 and pass original helper readback before installation.
Seven compressed auxiliary objects are bound to the exact tree and descriptor, then every original PLAN part and whole original digest is checked after decoding.
XZ reading reaches EOF after the expected original payload; the new truncation fixture confirms a missing trailer is rejected even if original payload bytes decode.
Only an owned temporary partial is installed by non-overwriting hard link; failure cleanup checks ownership and preserves the primary write failure when close also fails.
All fetches use no refmap, no tags, no FETCH_HEAD and no pruning; final refs/HEAD and absence of FETCH_HEAD are checked.
Helper path and exact source bytes are pinned; stable stat excludes atime and is checked before/after reading.

Archive byte transport success is separated from unchanged original archive-verifier success: archive_bytes_verified may become true, local_archive_verified and original_archive_verification_passed remain false.
No Lean command, remote ref update, MCP capture synthesis or new proof credit is present; full_p2_complete stays false.
Seven meaningful new local Git/XZ tests passed independently, using the frozen restored source; inputs were byte-identical before and after.

remaining_boundaries: The 7 tests use small synthetic local objects and XZ fixtures; they are not production archive evidence.
Actual download/assembly of the 409 production parts and seven auxiliary originals remains a separate root-owned execution gate.
The unchanged original repack verifier must still run against accepted source tree af74f02d263c72b0bb8e003ce49d1134ac04c5d5 after byte retrieval.
This review inspects retrieval and evidence-recording logic; it grants no new Lean or manuscript result.

resolved_review_notes.issue: An early draft compared complete stat_result including mutable atime.
resolved_review_notes.resolution: Frozen source uses the original helper stable fields dev/ino/mode/nlink/size/mtime_ns/ctime_ns; the frozen helper remains unchanged.

resolved_review_notes.issue: An early draft used local_archive_verified for byte-only retrieval.
resolved_review_notes.resolution: Frozen source reports archive_bytes_verified separately and explicitly leaves original archive verification unexecuted/unpassed.
